overview: Dalmore, Dail Mòr in Gaelic, is a hamlet and sandy bay on the Atlantic coast of Lewis, just north of Carloway. The beach faces north-west, a group of sea stacks stands at its north-east end, and on spring and summer evenings the low sun lights up the bay and cliffs. It lies in the Northside of Carloway.

There is more history here than first appears. Excavations after part of the sea wall collapsed in 1982 found Bronze Age structures and Beaker-period finds, including quartz arrowheads made from stone brought from the mainland. The cemetery behind the beach holds 18 war graves, and both feature in Peter May's Lewis novels. In August 2016 the Transocean Winner oil rig ran aground on the headland just off the beach.

Big Atlantic rollers often run into the bay and it is a long-standing favourite with surfers. It has a car park and public access, and the West Side Coastal Path passes through on its way from Gearrannan to Shawbost. Dalbeg, a smaller beach, is less than a mile along the coast. It's a good base for a day on the west side.

text: Dalmore faces north-west into the open Atlantic, so it picks up plenty of swell; large rollers frequently break on the beach. North-west swell is the most-cited ideal, and easterly winds blow offshore. The sand is shaped by the rocks at either end.

There is a strong rip current at the north end of the beach, and Visit Outer Hebrides warns of strong currents and huge waves in windy weather. Autumn to spring brings the most swell; check the forecast and local advice before paddling out.

Dalmore is an exposed reef break with lefts and rights. North-westerly swell with a north-easterly offshore is the best match. Watch out for dangerous rips. It's rarely crowded, can work at any time of year and spring has the cleanest days. Check the reef and tide before you paddle out.

cards.label: Level
cards.title: Intermediate+
cards.text: Powerful Atlantic surf. Not a beach for beginners on their own.

cards.label: Hazards
cards.title: North-end rip
cards.text: A strong rip runs at the north end; currents and waves get dangerous in wind.

cards.label: Crowds
cards.title: Usually quiet
cards.text: Local surfers turn up when it's good, but it's rarely busy.

practical.label: Parking
practical.title: Beach car park
practical.text: There's a car park by the beach. Keep the cemetery access clear.

practical.label: Facilities
practical.title: Basic
practical.text: Public access, a car park and picnic facilities; toilets by the car park. No showers.

practical.label: Lifeguards
practical.title: None
practical.text: Call 999 or 112 and ask for the Coastguard in an emergency.

practical.label: Nearby
practical.title: Dalbeg and Gearrannan
practical.text: Dalbeg beach is under a mile away; Gearrannan Blackhouse Village about 1.5 miles; Dun Carloway Broch under 3 miles.

practical.label: Check first
practical.title: Forecast and ferries
practical.text: Check swell, wind and CalMac or flight status if you are travelling that day.

faqs.a: Only in gentle conditions. There is a strong rip at the north end and strong currents and big waves in windy weather.
It is a beach for competent surfers. Beginners should go with a local instructor who can pick the right beach for the day.
Sea stacks at the north-east end, a cemetery with war graves, Bronze Age archaeology and the West Side Coastal Path.
Less than a mile along the coast.
